STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. The plate fills much of the frame, and the plate looks medium-large, so I estimate about 25 cm across.
b) Reference: the cherry tomato (3 cm) sits near the centre-bottom and the green beans are about 8-10 cm long. The plate width is roughly 8 cherry-tomato-to-bean lengths, consistent with about 24-26 cm.
Final width: about 25 cm square, so area = 625 cm².

- Green beans: a thin line, about 25 cm² footprint, about 1 cm thick, so about 25 ml. Chopped vegetables at 0.6 g/ml gives about 15 g.
- Cherry tomato: 1 piece, 15 g.
- Cooked meat (pork, seared, appears to be braised or roasted): covers about 20% of the plate, about 125 cm². Average thickness about 1 cm, so about 125 ml. At 1.0 g/ml this is about 125 g.
- Rice (white, with herbs): covers about 12% of the plate, about 75 cm², average thickness about 1 cm. Volume about 75 ml. Cooked rice at 0.8 g/ml gives about 60 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No substantial base layer is visible beyond the items above. The plate is only lightly loaded, so no large addition.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Spinach with carrot and dressing: about 45 kcal/100 g (dressing adds fat).
- Green beans: about 31 kcal/100 g.
- Cherry tomato: about 18 kcal/100 g.
- Cooked pork: about 250 kcal/100 g.

Totals: spinach 60 g → 27 kcal; beans 15 g → 5 kcal; tomato 15 g → 3 kcal; pork 125 g → 313 kcal; rice 60 g → 78 kcal. Total ≈ 426 kcal, about 275 g.
